articles.title: Assam Floods: 5.24 Lakh People Displaced Across 5 Districts - Whalesbook
articles.full_text:
Assam’s flood crisis has left over 5.24 lakh people displaced and 68 dead, with severe damage to nearly 49,000 hectares of cropland. The disaster impacts logistics, local infrastructure, and regional agriculture in Charaideo, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon, and Sivasagar.
Detailed Coverage
The flood situation in Assam remains severe, with the Assam State Disaster Management Authority reporting that over 5.24 lakh residents have been displaced across five districts. As of July 26, 2026, the death toll from the ongoing deluge has reached 68. The districts of Charaideo, Golaghat, Jorhat, Nagaon, and Sivasagar are currently facing the most significant impact from the rising waters.
Impact on Regional Agriculture and Infrastructure
The damage to agricultural land is substantial, with approximately 48,742 hectares of cropland submerged or destroyed. This loss of standing crops poses risks to local agricultural output and rural livelihoods in the affected regions. Beyond the immediate human toll, critical infrastructure—including state roads, bridges, and protective embankments—has sustained damage. Such destruction often leads to supply chain disruptions and increased costs for repairs, which can impact local economic activity in the short term.
Relief Efforts and Ongoing Risks
Administrative authorities have set up 354 relief camps to provide shelter to over 37,700 people. Joint rescue and relief operations are being carried out by the Army, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF). While these efforts aim to stabilize the immediate crisis, the Dhansiri river in Numaligarh continues to flow above its danger level, maintaining the risk of further inundation. With over 760 villages submerged, the recovery process for both the local population and the affected infrastructure will depend on the speed of the water receding and the subsequent assessment of structural integrity across transport networks and farmland.
